quarterly_data.signal: Schneider Electric unveiled Software-Defined Medium Voltage (MV) switchgear (which it calls the world's first fully software-defined MV switchgear): standardized, modular hardware platforms replace engineered-to-order custom designs, with functionality shifted into software and over-the-air updates with zero operational downtime. Based on Schneider Electric studies and estimations it delivers up to 3x faster ordering and manufacturing and up to 2x faster commissioning and onsite acceptance testing, with less wiring and fewer components. It is already deployed in the field through a pilot with Equinix in a live colocation data center. Schneider will extend the architecture across its medium voltage portfolio and progressively the rest of the powertrain, including PremSet and the AirSeT range (GM AirSeT, RM AirSeT, SM AirSeT). Pilot programs continue through 2027, with broader availability to follow in 2028. EVP Power Systems Melton Chang: 'Data centers are being asked to build faster than traditional power infrastructure can move.'
